# Free Lunch Lab / 不労所得研究所

> **There is such a thing as a free lunch.** An open, sourced list of apps that pay you basic income just for existing, in 7 languages. ／ 「タダ飯は、ある。」

- **Sourced and dated.** Every entry links to its official site and carries a "checked" month showing when its facts were last verified.
- **Risks included, hype excluded.** Each service states what you actually get, what it takes, the risks and how cashing out really works. No deposit schemes or promised returns.
- **Open-source code too.** The [open-source page](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/open-source/) lists the code behind basic income (protocols, wallets, proof of personhood, simulators), with stars and last commit fetched on every build. See [Open source projects](#open-source-projects).
- **A graveyard of dead programs.** Basic income schemes that ended are kept in the [graveyard](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/), each with a source.

**Disclosure:** some links on the site are the maintainer's referral links and are marked as such; the official link is always given too.

**Open data:** the visible services are published as JSON at [`data/services.json`](data/services.json) ([live](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services.json)) ended programs at [`data/graveyard.json`](data/graveyard.json) and open-source projects at [`data/open-source.json`](data/open-source.json), regenerated on every build (CC BY 4.0, referral links excluded).

⭐ **Star the repo if you find it useful**, and [contribute a service](CONTRIBUTING.md) you know about.

## About

Free Lunch Lab is a curated, multilingual list of apps and projects that pay you just for existing: basic-income-style schemes such as Ğ1, Circles, Gradido and Idena, plus a few point and cashback apps. Most of them verify that you are a unique human today; schemes for AI agents are welcome once they exist. Every entry also says whether it has been confirmed to work from Japan. The site is a static site in 7 languages (English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, German and Arabic) with a page per service and a list of basic income organizations.

- Live site: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev
- X: [@FreeLunchLab](https://x.com/FreeLunchLab)
- RSS: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/feed.xml (and `/{lang}/feed.xml`, generated from the update log)
- Source and data: this repository is public. Everything on the site is generated from [`src/data.js`](src/data.js), which you can reuse under CC BY 4.0 (see [License](#license)).

## Affiliate disclosure

Some links on the site are referral links or codes. If you sign up through them, the maintainer may receive a bonus. This never changes what you get, and every service that has no referral program is listed too. The tables below link to the site's own service pages, not to referral links.

## Badge

[![Listed on Free Lunch Lab](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/badge/listed.svg)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/badge/?ref=badge)

If your project is listed on the site, you're welcome to add a "Listed on Free Lunch Lab" badge to its README or website. It's free, and entirely optional. The [badge page](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/badge/) has a ready-to-copy Markdown and HTML snippet for every listed service, open-source project and organization, each linking back to its own page. The SVGs (`listed.svg`, `listed-light.svg`, `listed-card.svg`, `listed-card-light.svg`) are generated by `src/badge.js`, and every entry in `services.json` and `open-source.json` has a `badge` object with the snippet and target URL.

## How the repo is organized

- `src/data.js` — all content: services (`SERVICES`), categories, UI strings for every language (`T`), the update log, organizations, and the site URL
- `src/template.html` — the list page template (design and CSS)
- `build.js` — generates `public/`: the list page per language, a page per service and language, the organizations page, `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`; it also refreshes the tables in this README
- `og.js` — renders the share images (1200×630) with headless Chrome: one per language (`src/og/{lang}.png`), one per service and language (`src/og/svc/{lang}/{id}.jpg`) and one per essay and language (`src/og/essay/{lang}/{id}.jpg`), plus the favicon PNG/ICO and the 180px touch icon from `src/static/favicon.svg`. Fonts are subset to the characters used and embedded; images whose HTML and fonts are unchanged are skipped (`src/og/manifest.json`, `OG_FORCE=1` redoes all). `build.js` runs it after the font subsets are ready, retrying up to 3 times (progress is saved per image, so a retry resumes); `OG_SKIP=1` skips it
- `fonts.js` — self-hosted web fonts: `build.js` collects the characters each language actually renders per typeface and keeps woff2 subsets of them in `src/fonts/` (fetched once from Google Fonts with `text=`; new characters add a new file, existing files never change, `FONTS_REBUILD=1` starts over)
- `src/static/` — files copied to the site root as is (favicon, touch icon)
- `readme.js` — regenerates the badges, service table, organizations list, open-source tables and essay list in this README from `src/data.js`
- `data/` — `services.json`, `graveyard.json` and `open-source.json`, the open dataset written by `build.js` (also served at `/services.json`, `/graveyard.json` and `/open-source.json`); `open-source-cache.json` holds the last fetched GitHub/GitLab metadata so the build also works offline
- `oss-fetch.js` — fetches stars, last commit, archived status, license and language for the open-source list (`OSS` in `src/data.js`) from the GitHub and GitLab APIs into `data/open-source-cache.json`; `build.js` runs it first and keeps the cache on any network error (uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `gh auth token` if available, `OSS_OFFLINE=1` skips it). `src/oss.js` merges the list with the cache and flags projects as dormant after 12 months without a commit
- `liveness.js` — reach-tests every listed service's `official` URL and flags dead links and stale "checked" dates into `data/liveness-cache.json` (`403`/`429` count as live — a refused bot, not a gone page; `LIVENESS_OFFLINE=1` skips it; never fails the build). The companion list [awesome-molt-ecosystem](https://github.com/eltociear/awesome-molt-ecosystem) runs the mirror of this — it re-checks its *dead* entries for revival (reading this site's `/services.json` and `/graveyard.json`), while this checks the *live* ones for death
- `public/llms.txt` and `public/llms-full.txt` — an English index and full-text dump of the site for LLMs ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/) format), generated by `build.js` from the same data (served at `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`)
- `brand/github-social-preview.png` — 1280×640 social preview image for the GitHub repo (upload by hand in the repo settings)
- `brand/x/` — profile images for the X account and the script that renders them (not deployed)
- `src/worker.js` — a small Worker in front of the static files that counts page views in Workers Analytics Engine (see [Page view analytics](#page-view-analytics)); fonts, images and JSON skip it (`run_worker_first` in `wrangler.jsonc`)
- `public/` — build output, deployed to Cloudflare Workers (static assets)

URLs: `/` (English) and `/{lang}/` for the list, `/services/{id}/` and `/{lang}/services/{id}/` for each service, `/organizations/` and `/{lang}/organizations/` for organizations, `/verify/{method}/` and `/{lang}/verify/{method}/` for services by verification method (e.g. [World ID](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/verify/world-id/)), `/essays/` and `/essays/{id}/` (with language prefixes) for essays (data in `ESSAYS`), `/timeline/` and `/{lang}/timeline/` for a timeline of basic income experiments (data in `TIMELINE`; every item cites a source), `/open-source/` and `/{lang}/open-source/` for open-source projects (data in `OSS`, `OSS_GROUPS`), `/graveyard/` and `/{lang}/graveyard/` for ended services (data in `GRAVE`; only endings confirmed by an official or credible source).

## Build and deploy

```sh
node build.js       # writes public/, refreshes the README tables and runs og.js for missing or changed share images
npx wrangler deploy # publishes public/ to Cloudflare Workers
```

Maintenance: `node liveness.js` re-checks that every listed service still resolves and that no "checked" date has gone stale (run it periodically; it never blocks a build or deploy).

There are no npm dependencies; Node.js and, for the share images, Chrome are enough (without Chrome the build still finishes and warns about missing share images). The Chrome path can be set with the `CHROME` environment variable.

## Page view analytics

`src/worker.js` writes one data point per HTML page view (GET, status 200) to the Workers Analytics Engine dataset `free_lunch_lab_pageviews` (binding `PAGEVIEWS` in `wrangler.jsonc`). It records only:

| Column | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `index1` | language (`en`, `ja`, `zh`, `hi`, `es`, `de`, `ar`) |
| `blob1` | path (e.g. `/ja/shindan/`) |
| `blob2` | language |
| `blob3` | the `?s=` parameter (the tag on each X post; empty if none) |
| `blob4` | referrer host (`self` for links within the site, empty if none) |
| `blob5` | `1` if the user agent looks like a bot, else `0` |
| `double1` | `1` (one view) |

No IP address, user agent string, cookie, or referrer path/query is stored. Analytics Engine samples at high volume, so sum `_sample_interval` rather than counting rows.

Query it with the [SQL API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/analytics-engine/sql-api/). Create an API token with the **Account › Account Analytics › Read** permission, then:

```sh
ACCOUNT_ID=...   # Cloudflare dashboard → Workers & Pages → Account ID
API_TOKEN=...    # token with Account Analytics: Read

# views by path, last 7 days, bots excluded
curl -s "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/analytics_engine/sql" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \
  -d "SELECT blob1 AS path, SUM(_sample_interval) AS views
      FROM free_lunch_lab_pageviews
      WHERE timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '7' DAY AND blob5 = '0'
      GROUP BY path ORDER BY views DESC LIMIT 50"

# views by ?s= (X post tag), last 30 days, bots excluded
curl -s "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/analytics_engine/sql" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \
  -d "SELECT blob3 AS s, SUM(_sample_interval) AS views
      FROM free_lunch_lab_pageviews
      WHERE timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '30' DAY AND blob5 = '0' AND blob3 != ''
      GROUP BY s ORDER BY views DESC"
```

Add `FORMAT JSON` at the end of a query for JSON output (the default is tab-separated). Data is kept for 3 months.

## Adding a service

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the listing criteria first. Then add an entry to `SERVICES` in `src/data.js` and run `node build.js` (it also makes the new share images).

- `id`, `name` (Japanese display name), `nameEn` (optional, used for other languages)
- `cat` — category: `crypto-bi`, `app`, `pointsite`, `career`, `exchange`, `finance`, or `ai-agent` (for AI-agent basic income; a category with no entries never appears anywhere, so it shows up automatically with the first entry)
- `type` — `loop` (pays repeatedly) or `once`
- `global` — `true` if it works outside Japan; `onlyIn` (e.g. `us`) if only residents of one country can use it
- `ease` (1–5), `official` (official site), `added` (date, shows a NEW badge for 14 days)
- `checked` — month the facts were last verified, `"YYYY-MM"` (required for visible entries; shown as “Checked Oct 2026”)
- `ref` / `code` — referral link and code; `showCode: true` shows the code box next to the link; `codeOnly: true` when the code is entered in the app and the button points to the official page; `noRef: true` to list a service that has no referral program (an entry with neither `ref` nor `noRef` is hidden); `contactRef: { url, handle }` (with `noRef`) for a service whose referral code is not published but given by DM, with a per-language `contactRef` line that mentions the handle (shown on the card and page with the handle linked, and exported as `referralByDM` in services.json and in llms-full.txt)
- `verify` — how you prove who you are, an array of `{ "method": ..., "optional": true? }` with methods from `VERIFY` (`world-id`, `face`, `passport-nfc`, `kyc-id`, `phone`, `web-of-trust`, `ceremony`, `none`). Leave it empty if the entry’s own facts do not say which method is used. A page is built at `/verify/{method}/` for every method with 2 or more services (required first, then optional)
- `trust` — `cash`, `price`, `operator`, each `yes` / `partial` / `no` / `unknown` (`price: na` for non-crypto)
- `ja`, `en`, `zh`, `hi`, `es`, `de`, `ar` — `gain`, `note`, `need`, `caution` per language (English is the fallback); optional `warning` shows a highlighted box at the top of the service page, for strong warnings that should be read before signing up (start the `caution` with the same text so cards show it too)

Organizations live in `ORGS` (with `ORG_GROUPS` and `ORG_REGIONS`); set `svc` to a service `id` to cross-link the two pages.

## Adding a language

Add the language code to `LANGS` and a key for it in `T`, `CATS`, every service, `NEWS`, `PICKS`, `ORGS` (`desc`/`short`), `ORG_GROUPS` and `ORG_REGIONS` in `src/data.js`, then to `LANG_NAMES`, `LANG_TAG`, `OG_LOCALE`, `BODY_FONT`, `DISPLAY_FONT` and `SHARE_ORDER` in `build.js` and `FONTS` / `FACE` / `BODY` / `DISP` in `og.js`. The build stops if a UI string is missing.

## X profile images

`brand/x/avatar.png` (400×400, cropped to a circle by X) and `brand/x/header.png` (1500×500) are for [@FreeLunchLab](https://x.com/FreeLunchLab) and are not part of the site. Regenerate them with `node brand/x/render.js` (same Chrome and embedded-font pipeline as `og.js`).
